title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
content: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is an AI framework that enhances large language model (LLM) responses by incorporating relevant information retrieved from external knowledge sources. RAG combines the strengths of pre-trained language models with the ability to access specific information not included in the model's training data, helping to reduce hallucinations and improve factual accuracy.

title: LangChain Framework
content: LangChain is an open-source framework designed to simplify the development of applications using large language models (LLMs). It provides a standard interface for chains, integrations with other tools, and end-to-end chains for common applications. LangChain makes it easier to build context-aware reasoning applications.

title: Vector Databases
content: Vector databases are specialized database systems designed to store and efficiently query high-dimensional vectors or embeddings. They use similarity search algorithms like HNSW or IVF to find the most similar vectors to a query vector. Popular vector databases include Pinecone, Weaviate, Milvus, and FAISS.

title: Gemini LLM
content: Gemini is a family of multimodal large language models developed by Google. It can process and generate text, images, audio, and other modalities. Gemini comes in different sizes including Gemini Pro and Gemini Ultra, with varying capabilities and resource requirements.

title: Prompt Engineering
content: Prompt engineering is the process of designing and optimizing inputs to AI systems to achieve desired outputs. Effective prompt engineering involves understanding how to frame questions, provide context, and guide the model's reasoning process to improve response quality, relevance, and accuracy.

title: Machine Learning Algorithms
content: Machine learning algorithms are computational methods that enable systems to learn from and make predictions based on data. Common types include supervised learning (like linear regression, decision trees, neural networks), unsupervised learning (clustering, dimensionality reduction), and reinforcement learning.

title: Python Programming
content: Python is a high-level, interpreted programming language known for its readability and versatility. It's widely used in data science, machine learning, web development, and automation. Python's extensive library ecosystem makes it especially popular for AI development, with libraries like TensorFlow, PyTorch, and scikit-learn.

title: FAISS Vector Library
content: Facebook AI Similarity Search (FAISS) is an efficient library for similarity search and clustering of dense vectors. Developed by Facebook Research, it contains algorithms that search in sets of vectors of any size, even ones that don't fit in RAM. It's particularly useful for embeddings and is often used in RAG systems.

title: Neural Networks
content: Neural networks are a set of algorithms modeled after the human brain that recognize patterns. They interpret sensory data through machine perception, labeling or clustering raw input. The networks consist of layers of interconnected nodes or 'neurons' that process information using various activation functions.

title: Embeddings
content: In machine learning, embeddings are vector representations of data in a continuous space that capture semantic relationships. They convert high-dimensional categorical data into lower-dimensional numerical vectors. Word embeddings (like Word2Vec or GloVe) represent words in vector space where semantically similar words are positioned closer together.

title: Data Preprocessing
content: Data preprocessing involves transforming raw data into a clean, structured format suitable for analysis. This includes handling missing values, normalization, encoding categorical variables, feature scaling, and dimensionality reduction. Proper preprocessing is crucial for building effective machine learning models.

title: Transformer Architecture
content: The Transformer architecture is a neural network design that uses self-attention mechanisms to process sequential data. Unlike RNNs, Transformers can process entire sequences simultaneously, making them highly parallelizable. This architecture forms the foundation for models like BERT, GPT, and T5, revolutionizing natural language processing tasks.

title: API Integration
content: API (Application Programming Interface) integration involves connecting different software applications to enable them to exchange data and functionality. For AI applications, API integration allows systems to leverage external services for tasks like language translation, image recognition, or accessing specialized databases.

title: LLM Applications
content: Large Language Models (LLMs) have numerous practical applications including content generation, summarization, translation, sentiment analysis, code generation, conversational AI, and educational tutoring. When integrated with domain-specific knowledge, they can power specialized tools for legal, medical, financial, and other professional fields.

title: Tokenization
content: Tokenization is the process of converting text into smaller units called tokens. For natural language processing, tokens might be words, subwords, or characters. Tokenization is a fundamental preprocessing step for text analysis and is crucial for how LLMs process and understand language.
